sections.h2: Where is Syracuse, Utah, and what sits around it?
sections.html:
Syracuse is in northern Davis County, on the east shore of the Great Salt Lake, about 30 miles north of Salt Lake City. The city lies between the lake and Interstate 15, at an elevation of 4,272 feet, and covers about 10 square miles.

Neighbors are West Point to the north, Clearfield to the east and northeast, and Layton to the southeast. Syracuse calls itself the Gateway to Antelope Island, and a causeway off State Route 127 connects the city to Antelope Island State Park in the lake. It is part of the Ogden to Clearfield metropolitan area.

For a seller, the setting matters in two ways. Buyers like the lake and island access, and the land on the west side of town has wetlands that affect what can be built.

sections.h2: How did Syracuse grow from a farm town into a city?
sections.html:
Syracuse was settled in 1878 and took its name from Syracuse, New York, a city known for salt production in the 1800s. The town board formed in 1935, and a proclamation from Governor J. Bracken Lee made Syracuse a third-class city on September 13, 1950.

The growth since then is steep. Census counts show 4,658 residents in 1990, 9,398 in 2000, 24,331 in 2010 and 32,141 in 2020. The Census Bureau now estimates 39,909 for July 1, 2025. In 2020 the median age was 29.4 and 36.4% of residents were under 18, so the city is full of young families.

Much of the housing was built during that run of growth, so many houses are newer than in older Wasatch Front suburbs. Checking the age of the roof, water heater and furnace matters more than the age of the neighborhood.

sections.h2: What does the West Davis Corridor mean for Syracuse houses?
sections.html:
The West Davis Corridor, State Route 177, opened on January 6, 2024, and it runs northwest through Syracuse with interchanges at 2000 West and Antelope Drive. The first section is 16 miles long, from Farmington to West Point, and cost $750 million.

The road changed how people get around the west side of Davis County. It also changed interest in the land beside it. Syracuse is pursuing a 169-acre redevelopment area, the WDC Gateway Community Reinvestment Area, at Antelope Drive and 3000 West, for housing, retail and commercial use.

  • City manager Brody Bovero said the city saw a significant increase in interest after the highway opened.
  • The land is mostly farmed or undeveloped and needs wetland mitigation, which the city calls a significant hurdle.
  • UDOT plans a 2.5-mile extension north to 1800 North in West Point, with work expected to run from late 2025 to 2027.

Whether new development nearby helps or hurts a sale depends on the buyer. A cash buyer looks at the house as it stands today.

sections.h2: What is the climate like, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Syracuse has hot summers and a real winter. Summer highs often reach 95 degrees, the record high is 106 degrees on July 14, 2002, and the record low is minus 16 degrees on January 26, 1949.

The city averages about 24 inches of precipitation and about 39 inches of snow a year, and monsoon thunderstorms usually arrive from late July to mid-September. That mix means roofs, gutters and grading take a beating, and snow load and freeze-thaw cycles matter for older decks, driveways and sprinkler lines.

  • Check the roof and flashing after winter and after the monsoon season.
  • Look at grading near the foundation, since snowmelt and monsoon rain need somewhere to go.
  • Have the sprinkler lines blown out each fall before a hard freeze.

sections.h2: Which schools and neighborhoods do Syracuse buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Syracuse is in the Davis School District, and the city also has the Syracuse Arts Academy charter campuses. Syracuse High School opened in 2007, Syracuse Junior High dates to 1960, and elementary schools include Cook (1979), Syracuse Elementary (1968), Bluff Ridge (1999) and Buffalo Point (2008).

School boundaries are usually one of the first questions a family asks, so look them up when you list or talk to a buyer. The Syracuse Arts Academy campuses are public charter schools with their own enrollment.

Because the city grew so quickly, houses built in the same stretch of years tend to need the same work around the same time, such as roofs and water heaters.

sections.h2: What city rules could affect a Syracuse sale?
sections.html:
Syracuse regulates home businesses and temporary sales in chapter 10.35 of its city code, and those rules matter if you are clearing out a house. A garage or yard sale needs no license for up to three consecutive days, and you can hold up to four such events a year.

  • Minor home occupations are allowed in residential zones if they use no more than 300 square feet or 20% of the floor area.
  • Home occupation permits are not transferable and end when the applicant stops living at the address, so a buyer must apply again.
  • A business license is required unless the business is exempt under state law.

If you run a daycare, salon or similar home business out of the house, tell the buyer the permit does not carry over. For anything else, contact Syracuse City planning to confirm current rules.

sections.h2: How do Davis County property taxes work for a Syracuse seller?
sections.html:
Davis County property taxes follow the same Utah calendar as most counties: they are due November 30, and a late payment draws a 2.5% penalty or $10, whichever is greater, under Utah Code 59-2-1331. If November 30 falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date moves to the next business day.

The county mails a Notice of Assessors' Property Market Valuation at the end of July. The Davis County Commission acts as the Board of Equalization, and the county page gives September 15, 2026 as the late-appeal date, so file early.

  • You can appeal only the market value, not the tax rate.
  • Evidence can be closing documents, a certified appraisal, three or more comparable sales or proof of an error in the assessor's data.
  • Tax Administration is at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington, and can be reached at 801-451-3331.

Utah exempts 45% of a primary residence's value, up to one acre. Your title company prorates the current bill at closing.

sections.h2: What do Syracuse sellers usually need?
sections.html:
Syracuse is a city of owners, with 89.7% of homes owner-occupied and an average of 3.64 people per household. Sellers who contact us usually have a reason to move quickly, such as a job move, a divorce, a house that has outgrown the family or an inherited house nobody wants to keep.

A listing works well for a clean, updated house. If yours needs work, or you want to avoid showings and a long wait, a cash offer is a simple comparison. We buy as-is, you choose the closing date, and you can say no.

faqs.q: How many people live in Syracuse, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 39,909 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 32,141, so the city grew by more than 7,000 people in five years.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Syracuse, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Syracuse at $573,300 for 2020 to 2024. That is a survey estimate, not an appraisal of your house.

faqs.q: When are Davis County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30. If that date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day. After it, a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater, applies.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Syracuse property valuation?
faqs.a: Yes. Davis County mails valuation notices at the end of July, and the county page gives September 15, 2026 as the appeal deadline for that year. You can appeal only the market value, with evidence such as comparable sales or an appraisal.

faqs.q: Do I need a license for a garage sale in Syracuse?
faqs.a: No license is needed for up to three consecutive days, with a limit of four events per year, according to Syracuse City code chapter 10.35.

faqs.q: Will you buy a Syracuse house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to repair or clean before an offer. You can turn the offer down at no cost.
